newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Summit's Eggers would prefer modest gain.
newsitem.headline: Summit's Eggers would prefer modest gain.

text.p: Summit Gold NL Managing Director Alan Eggers said on Friday the company's recent drilling results in Queensland and in Central Otago had great potential, but that he would prefer to see a more modest gain in the share price.
Summit earlier said drilling results from its Valhalla project in northwest Queensland had revealed wide zones of uranium mineralisation.
The company has also had encouraging results from its gold prospect at Carrick in Central Otago.
The results boosted the share price to a peak of NZ$0.85 a share, up 47 cents from Thursday's close. At NZ$0.85, Summit was 1,064 percent higher than its low for the year of 7.3 cents.
By 1.15 p.m. (0015 GMT) the stock had backed down to NZ$0.65.
"I would choose not to make a comment on a specific price for the shares, but what I would say is that the results are significant," Eggers told Reuters from Perth.
Valhalla forms part of the Mount Isa Exploration Joint Venture, a 50/50 venture between Summit and Resolute Ltd. Resolute itself gained 14 cents to A$2.72.
"I prefer to see a much more modest increase in the (Summit) share price and for it to slowly climb over a period of time based on us delivering the results," Eggers said.
"It puts a lot of pressure on management to perform if the shares get out of whack with the true value of the company.
"It is very hard at the moment to put an absolute value on the company because to some extent we are dealing with potential," he said.
At Mt Isa, it was early days in what was potentially a huge discovery, and the same for its Central Otago operation.
"If all of those things come to fruition, well the shares could be worth considerably more than what anybody paid for them today," Eggers said.
"We've got to a lot of work. We've got the people and we've the money. We don't need to raise cash and we can afford to get on and do that job.

"I really don't like to see these things go too crazy," he said. "The market's having a bit of fun there but I would prefer to see it just a little bit more modest. With slow growth, everyone is the winner."
